parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The point P in Fig. 1.1 represents a point mass.

On Fig. 1.1, draw lines to represent the gravitational field around P.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A moon is in circular orbit around a planet.

Explain why the path of the moon is circular.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
Many moons are in circular orbit about a planet.

The angular velocity of a moon is *ω* when the orbit of the moon has a radius *r* about the planet.

Fig. 1.2 shows the variation of *r*³ with 1/*ω*² for these moons.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text:
Show that the mass *M* of the planet is given by the expression

*M* = gradient / *G*

where *G* is the gravitational constant.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use Fig. 1.2 and the expression in (c)(i) to show that the mass *M* of the planet is 1.0 × 10²⁶ kg.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the speed of a moon in orbit around the planet with an orbital radius of 1.2 × 10⁸ m.

figures.caption: Fig. 1.2
figures.alt: A gridded graph of r³ / 10²³ m³ against 1/ω² / 10⁷ rad⁻² s², with a straight line rising from the origin.
